Benefits decisions. Financial consequences.

Could your benefits gap
become an ACA penalty?

If you’re an Applicable Large Employer, offering a benefit isn’t the whole question. What you offer, who receives the offer, and what employees must pay can affect your exposure.

Know your status.

ALE status generally starts at an average of 50 full-time employees, including full-time equivalents, in the previous calendar year. Related employers may count together; seasonal-worker and new-employer rules can matter.

Know your coverage.

Offering minimum essential coverage to at least 95% of full-time employees and their dependents addresses one potential payment. Employees outside that offer—or coverage lacking minimum value or affordability—can still create exposure to another.

Know the trigger.

Either employer shared responsibility payment requires at least one full-time employee receiving a Marketplace premium tax credit. Workforce size alone does not trigger a payment.

Talk with Earl ↗
Before you decide

Get answers to the hard questions.

What if a traditional group health plan stretches our budget?

We can review available options and contribution arrangements. Telehealth and group life may address specific needs, but they don’t replace comprehensive medical insurance. We’ll make those differences clear.

What if employees already have health insurance?

Start by reviewing what they have and what your current benefits include. A separate telehealth program may duplicate existing services; group life addresses a different need.

Does choosing a higher tier settle our ACA obligations?

No tier label establishes compliance. Actual coverage, affordability, the employer’s offer, and applicable employer rules must be evaluated. A broader plan does not create a separate penalty exemption.

Can we review what we already offer?

Yes. Bring your current plan information and renewal concerns. We can compare your goals with the coverage, costs, and available alternatives.
